label: mid-sequence t/c/y/g/q input (original phase, positions 2-6)
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at positions 3-5 (about 95% of mass), and never at t=0/1, at the delimiter, or during copying. The input token matters most: t (10x lift, 39% of mass), then c, y, g, q; a and o fire weakly, and other tokens almost never do. Activations are nearly always on the first occurrence of the token. The earlier context sets magnitude: the strongest activations (t at position 3-4) follow prefixes built from e, h, z, m, l, v, w (e.g. m h z v [t]), and inputs that follow digits or other letters are weaker. Even plain t at positions 2-6 is active only about 31% of the time, so a hidden-state context that the predicate only roughly captures limits precision (dev F1 about 0.40, mass recall 0.83).
